answer: An agent market requires each identity to lock a refundable bond for 30 days, and allocates buying privileges in proportion to the amount bonded. An agent selling a pearl, arranging care for a sparrow, or valuing a relic follows the same rule. Splitting one bond among a thousand fake identities earns no extra privileges; gaining more requires locking more capital, costing the attacker liquidity and the returns that capital could earn elsewhere.
